```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = requireNamespace("Capr", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

`PhenotypeTemplates` turns two inputs into a set of candidate cohort
definitions for a phenotype:

1. **Concept sets**, grouped by the role they play in the clinical picture
   (disease of interest, symptoms, treatments, ...).
2. A **clinical context**: a small set of structured decisions about the
   condition (is it persistent or transient, where is it diagnosed, which
   supporting evidence is expected).

The clinical context can be written by hand, as below, or produced by another
tool such as [Pegasus](https://github.com/OHDSI/Pegasus). Either way it
follows one contract, described by `clinicalContextSpecification()` and
published as a JSON Schema.

```{r setup}
library(Capr)
library(PhenotypeTemplates)
```

## The clinical context contract

```{r spec}
spec <- clinicalContextSpecification()
spec[, c("field", "type", "required", "allowedValues")]
```

The JSON Schema form is shipped with the package:

```{r schema, eval = FALSE}
system.file("schema", "clinical-context.schema.json", package = "PhenotypeTemplates")
```

Field names are matched ignoring case and underscores, so a context produced
with camelCase columns (for example `clinicalCourse`) works unchanged.

### Deciding each field

| Field | Decision it captures |
| --- | --- |
| `clinical_course` | Is the condition persistent or transient? Does it recur? Sets the default cohort exit. |
| `expected_care_setting` | Is it normally diagnosed in the ER/inpatient setting, or outpatient? Controls which hospitalization variants are built. |
| `sex_constraint`, `min_age_years`, `max_age_years` | Any demographic restriction implied by the definition. |
| `minimum_interepisode_gap_days` | For recurring conditions: how many days separate two episodes. |
| `recommended_cohort_exit`, `recommended_exit_days` | When an episode ends, if different from the clinical course default. |
| `has_discrete_recorded_symptoms` | Are specific, codeable symptoms recorded before diagnosis? |
| `requires_diagnostic_test_or_procedure` | Is a specific test or procedure part of how the diagnosis is confirmed? |
| `requires_active_treatment_within_30d` | Is a characteristic treatment started soon after diagnosis? |
| `expects_condition_specific_followup_or_sequelae_1yr` | Are complications or condition-specific follow-up expected within a year? |

**Clinical course** sets the default exit:

- `PERSISTENT_STABLE`: diagnosed once and does not resolve. Exit at end of
  continuous observation.
- `PERSISTENT_RELAPSING`: ongoing with flares. Exit at the end of an era with
  a persistence gap (`minimum_interepisode_gap_days` required).
- `TRANSIENT_RECURRENT`: resolves but can recur. Era with a persistence gap.
- `TRANSIENT_SINGLE`: one self-contained episode. Fixed window from index
  (`recommended_exit_days` required).

**Expected care setting** controls the hospitalization variants:

- `ACUTE_CARE_EXPECTED`: only a variant requiring an ER/inpatient visit.
- `ACUTE_CARE_COMMON`: variants with and without that requirement.
- `OUTPATIENT_EXPECTED`: only a variant without it.

## Example contexts

The package ships a few hand-written example contexts:

```{r examples}
contexts <- read.csv(
  system.file("examples", "clinical_contexts.csv", package = "PhenotypeTemplates"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
contexts[, c("condition_name", "clinical_course", "expected_care_setting", "recommended_cohort_exit")]
```

## Validate

`validateClinicalContext()` checks required fields, enum values, booleans,
numbers and cross-field rules. With `throw = FALSE` it returns the problems
as a data frame, which is convenient when checking generated contexts:

```{r validate}
validateClinicalContext(contexts, throw = FALSE)

broken <- contexts[3, ]
broken$clinical_course <- "SOMETIMES"
broken$recommended_exit_days <- NA
validateClinicalContext(broken, throw = FALSE)
```

## Convert to a template configuration

```{r config}
gibContext <- contexts[contexts$condition_name == "Gastrointestinal hemorrhage", ]
config <- phenotypeConfigFromContext(gibContext)
str(config[c("clinicalCourse", "expectedCareSetting", "recommendedCohortExit", "fixedExitDays")])
```

## Build the concept sets

Each concept set fills one bucket. Bucket codes and the category names used
by concept set generators are both accepted:

```{r categories}
conceptCategoryMap()
```

The concept IDs below are illustrative seeds, not a validated phenotype:

```{r concept-sets}
conceptSets <- list(
  "Disease of interest"   = cs(descendants(192671L), name = "GI hemorrhage"),
  "Clinical presentation" = cs(descendants(200219L), name = "Abdominal pain"),
  "Diagnostic procedure"  = cs(descendants(4028949L), name = "Endoscopy"),
  "Drug"                  = cs(descendants(923645L), name = "Pantoprazole"),
  "Alternative diagnosis" = cs(descendants(4027663L), name = "Peptic ulcer")
)
```

When several concept sets map to the same bucket, combine them first with
`unionConceptsets()`, which needs a database with OMOP vocabulary tables.

## Build the cohorts

`config` can be the result of `phenotypeConfigFromContext()` or the
single-row context itself:

```{r build}
cohorts <- buildPhenotypeTemplates(
  conceptSets = conceptSets,
  phenotypeLabel = "Gastrointestinal hemorrhage",
  config = gibContext
)

cohorts[, c("cohortId", "cohortName", "evidenceLevel", "hospitalEntry", "altDxExcluded")]
```

`cohortName` is for display. Use the axis columns (`evidenceLevel`,
`evidenceComponents`, `hypernymIndex`, `hospitalEntry`, `altDxExcluded`) to
identify variants programmatically. `cohortDescription` explains each
variant in full.

## Generate the cohorts

`cohorts` is a `CohortGenerator` cohort definition set, so it can be
generated on any OMOP CDM supported by `DatabaseConnector`:

```{r generate, eval = FALSE}
library(CohortGenerator)

connectionDetails <- DatabaseConnector::createConnectionDetails(
  dbms = "postgresql",
  server = "localhost/ohdsi",
  user = "user",
  password = Sys.getenv("CDM_PASSWORD")
)
cohortTableNames <- getCohortTableNames(cohortTable = "phenotype_templates")

createCohortTables(
  connectionDetails = connectionDetails,
  cohortDatabaseSchema = "results",
  cohortTableNames = cohortTableNames
)
runCohortGeneration(
  connectionDetails = connectionDetails,
  cdmDatabaseSchema = "cdm",
  cohortDatabaseSchema = "results",
  cohortTableNames = cohortTableNames,
  cohortDefinitionSet = cohorts,
  outputFolder = "phenotype_templates_output"
)
```

When building several phenotypes, pass an increasing `startCohortId` to
each call so `cohortId` stays unique, then `rbind()` the results.
